items.text: Today marks four years since the death of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old woman from Saqez, after being detained by the morality police. Her death sparked widespread protests across Iran, and there has been no effective judicial accountability so far. The UN fact-finding mission stated that her death was caused by physical violence in detention and held the Iranian government responsible.

Shopkeepers and merchants in several Kurdish cities went on strike and closed their shops on the fourth anniversary of the government killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini. Videos showing closed shops in cities such as Sanandaj, Saqqez, Oshnavieh, and others have been released. The presence of military and police forces in some areas has also been reported.

Citizens report a sharp increase in prices of goods and services, difficulties in obtaining medicine, and insufficient wages. Teachers and workers also complain about harsh economic conditions and unpaid dues. The cost of living has risen significantly, causing serious problems for many families.

The parents of Hadis Najafi, a protester killed in the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests, joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. This campaign honors her memory and other victims of the popular uprisings in Iran. A video of this action was shared on social media.

On the fourth anniversary of Mahsa (Zhina) Amini's death, several shopkeepers and merchants in the cities of Baneh, Sanandaj, and Bukan went on strike and refused to carry out their daily activities. The strike took place on the 25th of Shahrivar. This action was taken as a form of protest against the current situation.

Lionel Messi has been called back to the Argentina national team for three friendly matches after his retirement. The matches are against Bolivia, Burkina Faso, and Benin. Messi's invitation may provide a final farewell opportunity with the fans.

Kioumars Heydari, deputy chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, stated that the Islamic Republic's armed forces are undoubtedly victorious in the war. He said Iranian missiles have caused serious damage to heavy US warships. He also added that Iran's strategic plans have led to the enemy's inactivity.

Human rights media reported the establishment of a security and military atmosphere coinciding with a general strike call in Kurdish areas of Iran. Videos show military convoys and riot units moving from Divandareh to Saqqez. This issue was discussed in an interview with Ovin Mostafazadeh, a human rights activist.

Amnesty International released a 1149-page report on the suppression of the "Women, Life, Freedom" protests on the fourth anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini's death. The report accuses the Islamic Republic of committing crimes against humanity. The Amnesty International Secretary-General stated that the evidence leaves no doubt about these crimes.

A retired armed forces member criticized the high cost of medicine in a video to Iran International. He said the government is taking money from the people to send medicine to Hamas and Hezbollah. These medicines are sent to Palestine and Lebanon.

Masoud Farhikhteh, a teachers' union activist, was sentenced to one year of imprisonment and additional punishments while serving his sentence in Karaj Central Prison. The sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj County. A new case was opened against him during his imprisonment.

Joseph Aoun, the President of Lebanon, announced that the country seeks an agreement with Israel. He said the agreement could pave the way for peace and the government wants to keep weapons under its control without causing internal conflict. He also requested help from Europe, the US, and Arab countries to support the Lebanese army to prevent a security vacuum after UNIFIL's withdrawal.

Bartina Koeman, wife of Ronald Koeman, former coach of the Netherlands national team, passed away at the age of 65 after a long battle with cancer. Ronald Koeman announced this sad news in a statement. The football community has also expressed condolences to his family.

Many people have postponed important life decisions such as marriage, medical treatment, and educational migration due to Iran's poor economic conditions. High living costs and inflation have forced people to focus only on daily survival without saving. Additionally, educational migration plans have been halted due to economic difficulties and the lack of required exams.

Videos published on social media show that the sister of Shirin Alizadeh, the mother of Hossein Farhi, and the mother of Atefeh Abed have joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." They honored the memory of the martyrs of the popular uprisings in Iran. This campaign is dedicated to commemorating the victims of public protests.

Mahmoud Rajabi called for the involvement of people, scholars, and the government in combating unveiled behavior. He emphasized the need to create conditions to counter hijab-related disorders and promote the culture of hijab. Rajabi warned that the enemy aims to attack culturally through unveiled behavior and stressed the importance of investing in this area.

Annis Kalamor, Secretary-General of Amnesty International, announced the identification of 87 officials and commanders of the Islamic Republic's security forces. These individuals should be prosecuted for crimes against humanity. This news was presented at Amnesty International's press conference in London.
A silent video received by Iran International shows the closure of shops and a strike by merchants in Oshnavieh city, West Azerbaijan province, on September 16.

Videos received by Iran International show that on September 16, shopkeepers in parts of the city of Mariwan in Kurdistan province were on strike. The strike was observed in some areas of the city. No further details about the cause or extent of the strike have been reported.

Abolfazl Qadyani, a political prisoner, rejected the government's narrative about the role of terrorists in the killing of protesters in December 2025 and held government forces responsible. He questioned why terrorists were absent from government rallies if they were responsible for the killings. Qadyani also named Ali and Mojtaba Khamenei as responsible for the killings.

Anis Kulamar, Secretary-General of Amnesty International, explained in the report on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death that the Iranian people face both repression by the Islamic Republic and the consequences of US and Israeli attacks. He added that the Iranian government has used these conditions to intensify repression and militarize public spaces.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi released a video about the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests and the national Iranian revolution in January 2026, emphasizing that the struggle for Iran's freedom continues. The statement noted that the voices of the fighters are heard from the heart of Iran, and four years after the killing of Mahsa Amini, the commitment to the struggle has been renewed. This fight extends from past uprisings to the Lion and Sun revolution.

The sisters of Babak Sadeghi Mohseni and the family of Behnam Ebrahimi joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." They honored the memory of these immortal individuals. This was seen in videos published on social media.

Mahsa Pirayi spoke at an Amnesty International meeting about her mother, Minoo Majidi's death, emphasizing that justice means accountability. She stated that responsibility should extend to the highest level of the command chain. These remarks were made on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death.

Mahsa Pirayi, daughter of Minou Majidi, spoke at the Amnesty International meeting in London. The event was held on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Mahsa Pirayi is one of the victims of the 1401 protests and the Women, Life, Freedom movement.

Rahim Molaeian, a painter and sculptor residing in Babol, was sentenced to six months of imprisonment by the Revolutionary Court of that city. He was charged with propaganda against the regime. The sentence was issued on September 12.

The Secretary General of Amnesty International in Germany called for judicial investigations into the suppression of protesters in Iran. He emphasized that the perpetrators have not been held accountable and Germany can initiate investigations using the principle of universal jurisdiction. Some victims residing in Germany can provide important evidence.

After the youth match between Sabouri Langarud and Abipoushan Rudsar, protests against the referee's decision led to physical assault. This incident caused the referee's eardrum to rupture. The head of Gilan Football Board announced the case is being pursued and requested action against the guilty coach.

A 10-year-old daughter of the late Ahmad Benvari sang for her father in the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. Ahmad Benvari was killed during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Dezful. The video has been shared on social media.

Austria's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned threats against journalists and emphasized support for media freedom. This stance followed statements by Abolfazl Shekarchi about staff of Iran International, BBC Persian, and Radio Farda. Other international reactions have also come from Germany and Canada regarding these threats.

The head of the judiciary in Rudan announced the suspension and cancellation of fuel cards for 163 vehicles that refueled more than once within 48 hours. This action was based on data from license plate recognition cameras and a judicial order. Smart monitoring of fuel stations continues, and vehicles with repeated irregular refueling will face legal actions.

Various individuals shared their feelings about the first time they went out without mandatory hijab. These feelings included liberation, power, freedom, and gratitude towards those who sacrificed their lives for this cause. Some also experienced comfort and a sense of life changing.

At least eight students at Birjand University have been temporarily banned from studying by the university's disciplinary committee. This ruling was issued by the disciplinary committee. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

Habib Farabbasi, Esteghlal's goalkeeper, will be sidelined for four weeks due to a groin injury. He will miss Esteghlal's match against Tractor in the eighth week of the Premier League. Aria Hosseinifard is the next option for Esteghlal in this position.

The first groups of athletes from various countries entered the Asian Games village in Nagoya, welcomed by Japanese ninjas. Iran's delegation includes over 300 athletes competing in 39 sports. The event took place in rainy weather.

Arash Azarmi from Iran International said China, the UAE, and Iraq are Iran's largest trading partners. The US is trying to limit ways to bypass sanctions by pressuring banks and foreign companies. He mentioned the gradual halt of CoinEx and restrictions on flights from Iran to Georgia.

On Wednesday, 24 Shahrivar, shopkeepers in Mahabad joined a strike on the fourth anniversary of the state killing of Mahsa Amini and closed their shops. This news is based on a video received by Iran International. The strike was held as a symbol of protest.

The Houthi group in Yemen announced that they targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu and an airbase in Khamis Mushait, Saudi Arabia, with dozens of ballistic missiles and drones. These attacks caused extensive fires and significant damage. They emphasized that they will continue their military operations deep inside Saudi territory.
Shopkeepers and merchants in Baneh city, Kurdistan province, closed their shops on Wednesday. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. They stopped working.

Hossein Ghashghaei, his wife Sara Shamsaei, and his brother Abolfazl Ghashghaei were arrested on September 9 by Ministry of Intelligence forces. They have been transferred to Arak, and their place of detention is unknown. Hossein Ghashghaei faces charges including propaganda against the regime and spreading false information.

Following the designation of the IRGC as a terrorist organization in Canada, there are concerns about the rejection of residency applications and deportation of Iranians who served their mandatory military service in the IRGC. About 200 Iranian specialists have written an open letter requesting attention to the situation of these individuals. This report was prepared by Mahsa Mortazavi.

Hassan Rodgar, detained in connection with the December 2025 protests, was transferred to Nowshahr prison to serve his one-and-a-half-year sentence. The sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court of Tonekabon. His transfer took place on the morning of Wednesday, September 15.

A video shows that the strike wave has reached the city of Kamyaran. Several shops and business units in this city in Kurdistan province have been closed. This information was reported by Iran International.

At dawn on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, at least one prisoner named Mehrdad was executed in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj. The prisoner had previously been sentenced to death for murder. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.

The campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" continues to honor the memory of those who died in January protests. Families light candles and recite the names of their loved ones to commemorate them. This was discussed in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.

The Swedish government summoned the Iranian ambassador and expelled one embassy official due to activities inconsistent with the Vienna Convention. The Swedish Minister of Justice described these activities as a threat to national security. The exact name and position of the expelled official have not been disclosed.

JD Vance, the US vice president, said the war with the Islamic Republic will enter a completely different phase within "the next one or two months." He also echoed Donald Trump's prediction that the war will end after the US midterm elections, without explaining whether the different phase means escalation, de-escalation, or diplomacy. Vance told the New York Post that no one can predict the future, but he thinks the president is right.

Reuters reported, citing informed sources, that US officials met with Houthi rebel representatives last weekend at the US embassy in Muscat. The unpublicized meeting was held with the help of the Omani government as a mediator.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry called the drone attack on Mecca by the Houthis an aggressive and shameful act. The ministry described it as a dangerous crossing of religious and ethical red lines. The Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council also condemned the attack and labeled it terrorist.

People shared their feelings about the first time they went out without mandatory hijab, including happiness, fear, courage, and stress. Some experienced a sense of liberation and freedom, while others initially felt fear that gradually diminished. For many, this experience was a mix of positive and negative emotions.

China's foreign minister met with Abbas Araghchi and urged Iran and the US to maintain rationality and restraint. He emphasized that China does not want regional tensions to spread to Yemen and the Red Sea. He also called on all parties to take effective measures to reopen the Strait of Hormuz quickly.
Videos and reports indicate a widespread strike in Sanandaj. Various parts of the city's market were closed on Wednesday. This information was published by Iran International.

Fars News Agency announced that Mahan Airlines flights from Iran to Turkey will be canceled from September 21, 2026, and to Oman from September 17, 2026, until further notice. The Georgian government will also stop all Iranian airline flights to Georgia starting next Monday. Sales of Georgia tours will continue until September 20.

Abbas Araghchi met with Wang Yi in Beijing and emphasized expanding Tehran-Beijing relations. He attributed regional conditions to attacks by the US and Israel and appreciated China's stance. Araghchi also expressed Iran's readiness to defend national sovereignty and welcomed diplomatic solutions.

Ali Nikzad said those who negotiated with the US had permission, and a detailed agreement was reached with Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz. He added that the US intended to destroy the country and government but did not recognize Iran's armed forces. Nikzad also stated that the Islamic Republic did not discuss enrichment in the negotiations and that talks will not continue if the US breaches the agreement.

The mother of Mohammad Khalili wept at the site of her son's killing in Isfahan and kissed the place where his body fell. Mohammad Khalili was killed by suppressors on January 8, 2026. He was 38 years old.

Four students at Iran University of Science and Technology were sentenced to a total of four semesters of suspension from studies by the university's disciplinary appeals committee. The suspension includes academic years as well. The ruling was issued by the disciplinary appeals committee.

Agnes Callamard, Secretary-General of Amnesty International, described the suppression of civil protests in Iran as a crime against humanity. She called on UN General Assembly member states to establish a people-centered mechanism to ensure justice in Iran. She also criticized the Security Council's inaction on this issue.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing that sholeh zard was cooked in memory of the immortalized. The dates 18 and 19 Dey were written on this traditional dessert. This act was done to commemorate two days of the 1404 government massacre.

The Swedish government expelled an employee of the Islamic Republic's embassy in Stockholm. The Swedish Ministry of Justice also summoned the ambassador of the Islamic Republic. This news was reported by Iran International.
Donya Veysi, a resident of Divandarreh, was arrested by security forces. She was transferred to an unknown location. This event occurred today.
Chris Wright, US Energy Secretary, said in a Fox News interview on Wednesday that about 18 million barrels of oil left the Persian Gulf on Tuesday, nearly equivalent to pre-war levels.

Ehsan Khandozi was appointed as the head of the economic working group of Mojtaba Khamenei's office. He will be responsible for maintaining the 60% share of economic cartels affiliated with the Supreme Leader's office in Iran's economy. Khandozi had previously authored a report that Ali Khamenei called nonsense.

Kioumars Heydari, deputy chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, stated that in response to any enemy action, a large number of missiles will be launched at the targeted area. He also threatened that if the war continues, some enemy forces will return to their countries while others will be destroyed in regional waters. Heydari emphasized that the armed forces rely on domestic capabilities and advanced technology.

On Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, coinciding with the fourth anniversary of the state killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini, the Aichi Cemetery road in Saqqez was blocked. A video showing this was published on social media. The cemetery is the burial place of Mahsa Zhina Amini.
A citizen shared a video showing closed shops in Thalath Babajani, Kermanshah province. He says the shopkeepers have joined a strike. The video was sent on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar.

On the evening of Wednesday, September 16, coinciding with the anniversary of the state killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini, motorcyclists and government forces established a security atmosphere in the streets of Tehran. This was observed in videos received by Iran International.

Egypt condemned the Houthi drone attack attempt on Mecca and stated that Saudi Arabia's security is an integral part of Arab countries' national security. The Palestinian Authority also condemned the attack and called the security of Saudi Arabia and the holy sites a red line. Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned the attack and expressed support for Saudi Arabia.

As the official opening of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games approaches, issues with athlete accommodation and transportation have been reported. The South Korean men's basketball team criticized the small rooms and short beds. Additionally, buses carrying the South Korean and Qatari football teams lost their way and arrived late at the stadium.

Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, emphasized the need to maintain freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab according to international laws. He condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and obstacles to navigation in Bab al-Mandab. Guterres also called for serious negotiations to end the conflicts in Yemen and the Middle East.

Forough Kenani said that Prince Reza Pahlavi's message narrates the protests from 2016 to today as a continuous path of Iranian people's struggles. The message emphasizes national solidarity, Iranian identity, and political responsibility toward the victims. The role of families seeking justice in preserving the memory of the victims and preventing the forgetting of repression is also highlighted.

Sadeghollah Shafiei, a citizen of Kamyaran, was arrested on September 9 after being summoned to the intelligence office of the city and transferred to an unknown location. There has been no news about his condition so far. His detention continues.

A citizen sent a video showing dandelions being released near Khayyam's tomb in Nishapur on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death. This event took place on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar. The video was sent to Iran International.

Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, expressed concern about human rights violations in Iran and the death penalty. He described the situation of women in Afghanistan as intolerable and said the UN is trying to pressure the Taliban. Guterres stated that restrictions on women in Afghanistan threaten the country's progress.

A video shows that on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, police vehicles were stationed in the streets of Urmia. This coincided with the anniversary of the state killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini. The video was released by Iran International.

Rafael Lusan announced that the agreement to extend Luis de la Fuente's contract with the Spanish national team until the 2030 World Cup is nearing completion. The new contract will place de la Fuente among the top five highest-paid national team coaches. De la Fuente has won three major championships so far.

Jean-Yves Le Drian, the French foreign minister, commemorated the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death and emphasized that her death echoed the slogan "Woman, Life, Freedom" in Iran and worldwide. He stated that the Iranian government's repression cannot silence this cry and that France stands with the Iranian people for justice and dignity. Le Drian also called for Iranians to freely decide their future.

The mother of Siavash Mahmoudi, a teenage protester killed in the 2022 uprising, released a video. She stated that she will seek justice for her son's blood until her last breath. This statement was made on the anniversary of Siavash's death.

The foreign ministers of Turkey and Iran discussed diplomatic efforts to end conflicts. Hakan Fidan emphasized continuing negotiations and the importance of maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. These talks aim to ensure regional energy security.

Shahad Alavi from Iran International referred to the strike in Kurdish cities marking the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Jina Amini's death, showing the persistence of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. He said the strike alone will not change the government but is part of a process demonstrating the community's strength and solidarity. The spread of strikes to other parts of Iran could indicate the formation of a widespread will to protest.

Amnesty International has called for the establishment of an international criminal mechanism to address crimes against humanity during the suppression of the 1401 protests. The organization has requested the Security Council to refer Iran's case to the International Criminal Court. It also urged the UN General Assembly to create a special mechanism if the Security Council reaches a deadlock.

Sadaf Baghbani, a victim of the Women, Life, Freedom movement, said the movement broke fear and paved the way for continued protests. She described the experience of repression and violence as changing the meaning of life and security for protesters. Baghbani called for continued support for the victims and prisoners of this movement.

Fatemeh Jami, a citizen of Gorgan, remains in Gorgan prison without a judicial decision after 79 days of detention. Her case is still unresolved and no court session has been held for her. The possibility of temporary release on bail has not been provided.

Hatam Ahmadi, CEO of Fajr Sepasi club, announced that Alireza Beiranvand's transfer to the team is confirmed. The only remaining issue is determining the exact time of his military service enlistment. Beiranvand must join Fajr Sepasi, but he cannot be used until mid-season.

A video dated Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, shows a long line of cars in the city of Sarakhs, Khorasan Razavi province, waiting to receive gasoline. The video was sent to Iran International. The issue relates to gasoline shortage or demand in this area.

The Instagram page of the German Embassy in Tehran commemorated the fourth anniversary of the killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini. The American Jewish Committee also wrote that she died in hospital after being detained by the morality police for not observing the hijab. The organization emphasized that her death has become a global symbol of women's repression and human rights violations.

Navid Khoshnezhad, a citizen from Izeh, was released from Ahvaz prison after posting a 10 billion toman bail. His lawyer stated that she is still unaware of the charges against him. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Today marks the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. On this day, routes leading to Aichi Cemetery in Saqez were blocked, and merchants in 13 cities including Saqez and Sanandaj went on strike. Security forces' presence in Saqez has also increased.

After a strike in Kurdish cities, a security atmosphere has been established. Mahan Airlines flights to Turkey and Oman have been canceled. This was mentioned in the audio version of Titraval with Niousha Saremi.

The US Treasury Department held a meeting with international financial institutions to advance the economic exclusion operation. The goal is to isolate Tehran and limit its ability to finance the war in the Middle East. Necessary information to cut off revenue streams related to the Iranian government was provided during the meeting.

Reuters reported that American officials met with Houthi representatives in Oman. CENTCOM also confirmed a secret meeting between military commanders from the US, Israel, and eight Arab countries to discuss the war in Iran. This information was sourced from five informed officials.

Ange Postecoglou, Al Nassr's coach, defended Cristiano Ronaldo after their 4-0 loss to Al Ain. He said the responsibility is his but Ronaldo remains a role model and the players gave their best. Al Nassr suffered Ronaldo's heaviest defeat in Saudi Arabia in the AFC Champions League.

The Alaj website, created to identify opponents of the Islamic Republic abroad, has gone offline. The reason is unclear and may be due to domain blocking or technical issues. The technical team stated that due to high traffic and cyberattacks, the site was temporarily taken offline.

The third session of the trial of Mehran Mohagheghi, accused of driving a car into a crowd at an Iranian protest in Richmond Hill, ended without a verdict. The incident occurred on May 10 in Richmond Hill, Toronto, and Mohagheghi was arrested after causing damage and threatening attendees. The case is still ongoing.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad said the Women, Life, Freedom movement was an exceptional revolution that became a turning point in the history of the Islamic Republic. He added that the consequences of this movement, from increased repression to subsequent developments, stem from the government's response to the 1401 protests. He also noted that the repression of protests and the return of security figures indicate a change in the Islamic Republic's approach after this movement.

At least 300 faculty members of Farhangian University have not received their salaries for over a year and are in an uncertain employment status. Some of these professors are protesting forced retirement. This state of uncertainty continues.

American diplomats met with Houthi representatives in the US embassy in Muscat to discuss tensions in the Red Sea. The talks focused on continuing the ceasefire and ensuring the Bab al-Mandeb Strait remains open. Houthi representatives stated their attacks target only Saudi ships.
This news refers to Russia's role in the Islamic Republic's attack on the US base. No further details about this role are provided. The topic discusses Russia's influence in this attack.

Amin Shirafkan and Alireza Hajtemand were arrested by security forces in Gorgan. The arrest took place on the morning of Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, at Shirafkan's workplace. Both were transferred to the Gorgan police detention center.

A citizen sent a video on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, showing ready-to-distribute food containers. He stated that he is distributing these foods among the needy in memory of the martyrs of the Mahsa uprising.

Workers' wages are equivalent to the cost of living for only eight days. This indicates a significant gap between income and living expenses. The livelihood of workers is severely affected by this issue.

Reza Pahlavi, on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death, stated that the Iranian nation is in a new phase of struggle to reclaim Iran. He mentioned the deaths of other protesters and described recent uprisings as part of the revolutionary path. Pahlavi emphasized that the current opposition solidarity is the result of a long and costly journey and vowed to continue the path of the deceased.

Esteghlal club will form a women's volleyball team with Niloufar Hojati as head coach. Hojati was a coach for the Iranian women's national volleyball team in the 2026 Asian Championship. Additionally, Esteghlal has reached an agreement with Fatemeh Khalili, a player of the Iranian women's national volleyball team.

Air traffic control tower staff across the country went on strike from the evening of Tuesday, September 14 to the night of Wednesday, September 15. This strike caused widespread disruption and several hours of delay in flights. Pilots in some cases waited between half an hour to two hours to receive clearance from the control tower.

The third edition of the international film festival "Woman, Life, Freedom" began on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Unlike previous years, this edition is not limited to one city and is held in various locations worldwide. The festival is also held online to reach a wider audience.

Wang Yi, China's foreign minister, during a meeting with Abbas Araghchi, called for restraint from Tehran and Washington and a swift return to the Islamabad understanding. He also emphasized the need for the rapid reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring the security of international waterways. The Chinese foreign minister stated that China will continue efforts to establish peace and stability in the Middle East.

Siamak Aram stated that the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement has helped form more cohesive networks among the Iranian diaspora. This movement has facilitated coordinated gatherings and activities in various cities worldwide. Additionally, diaspora activities have changed Western officials' rhetoric, but this change has not yet translated into practical policies.

Antonio Guterres condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and disruptions in shipping routes. He emphasized the need to maintain freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab according to international law. Guterres warned that the escalation of the crisis could have broader security and humanitarian consequences.

The foreign ministers of Israel and Morocco agreed in a trilateral meeting with the US ambassador to the UN to enhance bilateral relations. The agreement includes upgrading diplomatic representations, increasing flights, and holding high-level meetings. They also agreed to finalize agreements on investment protection and double taxation prevention by the end of 2026.

A citizen stated in a video to Iran International that after an accident, they need to buy a car radiator for seven million tomans. This indicates the rising inflation in Iran. The price of car parts has increased significantly.

Turkish and Pakistani officials stated that Saudi Arabia has not requested help from these two countries following intensified Houthi attacks. The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure are the first test of the new defense pact among these countries. The Houthis have denied targeting Mecca.

The CENTCOM spokesperson stated that the US military has achieved its objectives against the Islamic Republic and weakened Iran's missile and drone capabilities. He said the Iranian navy is practically destroyed and Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, the main shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared and are open.

AC Milan lost 2-0 to Benfica in their first match of the new Europa League season. Benfica won at San Siro against Milan for the first time in their history. Goals by Dodi Lukebakio and Kaminski led to this defeat.

Manchester United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the third round of the English League Cup and was eliminated. This is the first time in 50 years that Manchester United has lost at home after leading by two goals. Some fans stayed in the stadium after the match and protested.

A citizen reported that the Tehran to Sulaymaniyah flight was delayed at Imam Khomeini Airport due to lack of flight clearance. The pilot stated that because there is no radar in the country, they have to estimate the route, causing delays in issuing the clearance.

Mahan Airlines has suspended its international flights to Turkey and Oman until further notice. This decision was made after the United States imposed new sanctions on Mahan Air's support network. The news was reported in an interview with Amir Giti on Iran International.

Four years after the killing of Mahsa Jina Amini, Iranian women have reclaimed part of their right to choose in the streets, but this right is not yet guaranteed by law. Women discuss their experience of going out without a headscarf and the costs they have paid. This topic was covered in the September 16 special program on Iran International.

The American company Poweras has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Pakistan Army and received an initial order related to unmanned aerial systems. This news was released simultaneously with a delegation from Poweras meeting the Pakistan Army commander. Details of the order or the type of unmanned systems were not disclosed.

Barcelona defeated Racing Santander 7-2 in the sixth week of La Liga. The team recorded its seventh consecutive win in seven official games this season and set a new record with 28 goals in the first six weeks. Rafinha scored a hat-trick and leads the La Liga top scorers.

During the first week of Iran's League One football match between Basat Kermanshah and Naft o Gaz Gachsaran, referees' belongings including mobile phones, gold, and cash were stolen from the locker room. The stolen items were valued at over 500 million tomans. This incident caused a 40-minute delay in the game, and after the match, the referees left the stadium without compensation.

The US embassy in Yemen reiterated its support for the internationally recognized government of Yemen. Jonathan Hop confirmed Washington's support in talks with Yemen's foreign minister. The US stands with the Yemeni government against attacks by the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic.

Shahad Alavi from Iran International said the recent Amnesty International report attributes responsibility for repression to local and provincial officials as well. The report shows that being part of the command chain can create legal responsibility. It is no longer possible to avoid accountability by arguing that one was not directly involved in the repression.

The US House of Representatives approved a bill extending the Iran Sanctions Act (ISA) until the end of 2031. Currently, the law is valid until the end of 2026, and its extension maintains the legal framework for sanctions on parts of Iran's economy. This bill will take effect after the US president signs it.

Donald Trump will meet with Gulf leaders next Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The main focus of the meeting is to discuss the US strategy after the war with the Islamic Republic. Foreign ministers of the six GCC countries will attend the session.

Choo Hyun, South Korea's foreign minister, stated that Seoul has not yet decided on sending military forces to the Strait of Hormuz. These remarks were made on Thursday, September 17. He made these comments before traveling to Washington.

ABC News, citing a US Department of Homeland Security intelligence bulletin, reported that the Islamic Republic likely intends to target the industrial control systems used by American energy companies to monitor storage tanks in cyber attacks. According to the bulletin, such attacks could lead to physical damage or fuel and chemical leaks. The US Department of Homeland Security also stated that Iranian cyber actors used DeepSeek AI in early August to research storage tank capacities in the United States.

Joe Wilson, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, welcomed the passage of the 'Lindsey Graham 2026 Russia and Iran Sanctions Act'. The House passed the bill on Wednesday with 262 votes in favor and 159 against, sending it to President Donald Trump for signature. The legislation extends the authorization of Iran sanctions until 2031.

Yasmin Ansari commemorated Mahsa Jina Amini on the fourth anniversary of her death. She mentioned the killing of thousands of protesters, political prisoners, and executions. Ansari emphasized continuing the fight for freedom and human rights in Iran.

Anwar Ibrahim, the Prime Minister of Malaysia, condemned the interception of a drone near Mecca, calling it a threat to the security of the holy city. He praised Saudi Arabia for its swift action to protect Mecca and called for restraint and dialogue. The Saudi-led coalition destroyed the drone and attributed the attack to the Houthis, who denied involvement.

Times of Israel reported that the Lod District Court sentenced Alexander Granovsky, a resident of Petah Tikva, to 13 and a half years in prison for espionage, property destruction, and arson on behalf of the Islamic Republic. According to the report, in exchange for money from an Iranian agent, he set nine cars on fire, wrote anti-government slogans, and surveilled the neighborhood where former Israeli Defense Minister Benny Gantz resides. The Central District Attorney's Office declared this the heaviest punishment yet for acting on behalf of Iran.

The economic crisis caused by the war in Iran has forced thousands of Afghan migrants to return to their country. Sharp price increases and the devaluation of the rial have wiped out much of their savings. More than two million Afghans have left Iran in the past two years.

Reuters reported that the number of cargo ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday dropped to 3 vessels. This is significantly lower than the daily average of about 17 vessels over the past 10 days. The data is based on shipping information.

The New York Times reported that US intelligence officers expressed concern about possible Chinese espionage in the potential $24 billion sale of dozens of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia has decades of military cooperation with the US, but it buys ballistic missiles from China and the Chinese military helps Riyadh build missiles. A Pentagon report stressed that only Saudi and American officers and contractors should have access to sites where F-35 technology is kept.

The US House of Representatives approved a five-year extension of Iran sanctions law, including restrictions on investment in the energy sector and provision of goods and services to oil and petrochemical industries. This law is considered the oldest pillar of Iran's energy sanctions. According to Miad Maleki, this law deters major oil companies like Shell and Total from entering Iran's refining sector.

Mojtaba Yousefi stated that rising oil prices can act as a deterrent against the US, but some officials' stances have led to a decrease in oil prices. He described oil prices as a decisive factor in the resistance axis. Regarding the Islamabad agreement, he said staying in the deal after the US withdrawal is neither dignified diplomacy nor wise.

Amir Giti stated that the Iranian government will retreat from Trump's demands only if its financial resources and economic interests are at risk. He added that economic pressure has increased but the government has not yet yielded. These remarks were made regarding the Islamic Republic's willingness to negotiate and the impact of economic pressures.

Shayan Samiei referred to a CNN report about the possible transfer of Russian satellite information to Iran before the attack on Prince Sultan base. If this cooperation is confirmed, Russia's role will go beyond political support and military cooperation. Moscow would effectively enter Iran's intelligence and targeting chain.

The documentary "Naza," shown at the Venice Film Festival, presents the accounts of 24 Israeli officers and soldiers about military operations in Gaza. It claims an attack was approved with the anticipation of killing 500 civilians, which the Israeli army has denied. The film has sparked debate about the army's conduct and freedom of expression in Israel.
Abdolbaset Bapiri, a citizen from Oshnavieh, was arrested by security forces in Piranshahr on Tuesday, September 14. He was transferred to an unknown location. No further details have been released.

Peyman Falsafi, Tehran representative, stated that the Islamic Republic will neutralize any US military threat with faith and hidden defensive capabilities. He added that economic sanctions have strengthened the will of the Iranian nation. The enemy fears entering a military war due to Iran's defensive capabilities.

A video shows the situation of Fly Kish passengers in Istanbul after the sanctions on Iranian airlines. Passengers had to board the plane from an underground corridor early Thursday morning. This occurred outside the usual area and conditions of Istanbul Airport.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated at the Iranian University Professors' Assembly that with inflation over 60 to 70 percent, a 20 percent salary increase is insufficient. He highlighted economic problems and inflation, noting there is no simple solution. He also expressed hope that the enemy will adhere to the commitments made in the memorandum of understanding.
A video showing the deployment of officers on a street in Shiraz has been released. The video depicts a security atmosphere in the city. The video is silent.

Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in the Campeones Cup final, where his team defeated Cruz Azul 2-0. Messi also assisted Casemiro's goal. This championship marks Messi's 49th professional career title.

Rouhollah Rahimpour commented on Trump's statements about Iran's willingness to reach an agreement and the possibility of ending the war before the midterm elections. He said that changing the timing of the war's end does not necessarily mean a change in goals or reaching an agreement. He also emphasized that it cannot be said with certainty that the government has decided to end the war through an agreement.

Amir Ghalenoei announced the first list of Premier League players for the national football team after the World Cup. In this list, Mohammad Hossein Kanaani Zadegan and Roozbeh Cheshmi, the two captains of the rival teams, are absent. Three goalkeepers and several defenders and midfielders have been invited to the national team.
